data.title: Unquoted Service Paths Permit Privilege Escalation
data.summary:
Services were configured with unquoted executable paths containing spaces, in directories
writable by standard users, allowing a standard user to have their own executable run as
SYSTEM at service start.
data.description:
When a service path contains spaces and is not quoted, Windows attempts each successive
interpretation of the path in turn. An executable placed at an earlier interpretation runs
instead of the intended one, with the service's privileges.

Exploitation requires both the unquoted path and write access to one of the intermediate
directories. Either alone is harmless, which is why scanners that report every unquoted
path produce noise — the finding is the intersection, and that is what should be reported.

It typically appears with older or in-house software whose installer did not quote the
path, and it persists for years because nothing revisits service configuration.
data.recommendation:
* Quote the executable path of every affected service.
* Correct permissions on the intermediate directories so standard users cannot write to
  them, which removes the exploitability independently of the path.
* Audit service paths and their directory permissions together, so remediation is scoped to
  the services that are actually exploitable.
data.short_recommendation: Quote service paths and remove user write access to their directories.

attack_techniques.technique: T1574.009 — Path Interception by Unquoted Path
